transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I… I came because since my wife’s fall, I haven’t really been myself. I used to be organized, had lists, kept things moving. Now I sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart, and I’ll either start crying or snap over some tiny thing.

Bills are piling up, the housework’s not getting done, I’ve missed mentoring calls… it’s like I just can’t make myself function the way I used to.
How long have you been feeling this way since your wife's fall?
About two months now… since the fall. That’s when everything at home changed.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure, really. I haven’t been doing much of anything I used to enjoy, so… it’s hard to say.
Do you feel guilty about anything related to your wife's fall?
I… I don’t know. I’ve gone over it in my head, but I’m not sure I’d call it guilt. It’s just… hard not to think about.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?
I don’t really know. I haven’t been keeping up with much, so it’s hard to tell if I’ve lost interest or just… haven’t had the chance.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?
Not really sure. I can’t think of much I’ve been enjoying lately… I haven’t really tried.
Are there things that you used to enjoy that you've actually tried to do since your wife's fall?
I don’t think so. I mean… nothing really comes to mind that I’ve actually gone and done. I’ve mostly just let things sit.
Do you feel sad most of the time?
Yes… a lot of the time. Since my wife fell, I’ll just sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart and… sometimes I end up crying. I’m not really myself.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your wife's fall?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been checking… my clothes feel about the same, I think.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself since your wife's fall?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I haven’t… made any plans or anything like that. It’s more just been hard, I suppose.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling restless and unable to sit still since your wife's fall?
I don’t know… I haven’t really paid attention to that. I suppose I sit a lot, but I couldn’t say if I’m slower or restless exactly.
Do you feel worthless?
I… I don’t know. I try not to think about myself that way. It’s not something I really have an answer for.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to?
I’m not really sure. I guess I haven’t been watching myself that closely… maybe I sit around more, but I don’t know if I’m actually moving slower.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since your wife's fall?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been weighing myself or anything… my clothes seem about the same, I think.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself?
I… don’t really know how to answer that. I haven’t made any kind of plan or anything. It’s just… not something I want to get into much.
Do you feel like you're resting or sitting still more often than you used to?

Yes… I think so. I spend a lot more time just sitting at the kitchen table, looking at her medication chart and not really doing anything. Things are piling up, and I just… can’t seem to get myself moving like I used to.
Do you feel like your emotional pain is overwhelming most of the time?

Most of the time… yes. Since my wife’s fall, I don’t feel like myself. I used to be the one with lists and a plan, and now I just sit there at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. Sometimes I cry, sometimes I snap over nothing… and things just pile up because I can’t seem to make myself function.
Have you tried to do things you used to enjoy since your wife's fall, but found that you didn't enjoy them as much as you used to?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really tried much, to be honest. Things I used to do just… haven’t been on my mind.
Have you experienced a lack of pleasure in activities that you used to find enjoyable since your wife's fall?
I don’t really know. I haven’t been doing much of anything I used to enjoy, so… it’s hard to say if I’d still enjoy it or not.
Have you been feeling this way for more than two months?
About two months, yes… since my wife fell and everything at home changed.
